title: Does TradingView's aggregate Technical Rating (Buy/Sell/Neutral basket) predict next-day moves?

tables.name: 5-day forward edge by signal (present vs absent)

notes: Prompted by github.com/atilaahmettaner/tradingview-mcp. Rating replicated from real OHLCV history (5 oscillators + 5 moving averages, TradingView's own published methodology, since the live rating itself isn't backtestable -- no historical query support). tv_strong_buy sign-flips TRAIN +0.46% -> VAL -0.26% (present win rate also drops below absent's on VAL, 48.1% vs 52.6%) -- the classic overfit signature this project's whole testing discipline exists to catch. tv_oscillators_bullish sign-flips the OTHER direction (TRAIN -0.21% -> VAL +0.31%) -- still a flip, still disqualifying. tv_buy_or_better doesn't flip on avg return (TRAIN +0.19%/VAL +0.35%, both positive) but fails the win-rate half of the bar on TRAIN (present 53.7% < absent 54.8%) -- a bigger-but-less-consistent trade-off this project has rejected elsewhere. random_control itself sign-flips train-to-val too (+0.25% -> -1.07%), confirming the harness is behaving sanely.

conclusion.summary: None of the 3 real signals clear the bar (beat baseline on both win rate AND avg return, on both splits). 2 of 3 sign-flip train-to-val outright; the third fails the win-rate consistency check on train. Matches the outcome of every other classic single-family technical-indicator signal tested in this project (Bollinger, Fibonacci, MACD/EMA, VWAP/ORB) -- confirms the pre-registered expectation, closed.
